feature: Segmented thumb: lighter glass that morphs
summary: Every segmented control's thumb is now a lighter pane of Liquid Glass on a darker, recessed rail, easy to see in light and dark. Picking another option stretches the glass over both options, then it settles a few points past and back. You can also grab the thumb and drag it.
setup: Photonz Probe, release Next, no switch changed from its default. Walk: Scripts/playtest/segmented-thumb-glass-walk.json (its drag needs the Mac to itself).

try.do: Put down a text label, pick it, and look at Across and Down in the Text section (dark).
Switch the Mac to light and look at the same rows.
Click Center, then Right, then Left, quickly, and watch the glass travel.
Press on the picked segment and drag the thumb sideways, then let go over another one.
Open a recording and look at View | Edit in the title bar.
Press Cmd-2 and watch the thumb go over to Edit (dark).
Compare with the component page's Sizes section in light and dark.

evaluate: Can you find the picked option at a glance now, in both light and dark?
Is the light rail too heavy a grey on the light panel, or is the extra depth right?
Does the stretch-then-settle read as liquid glass, or would a plain glide feel better?
Is 420ms right for the move, or does it feel slow on a quick run of clicks?
Does dragging the thumb feel like it belongs, or is clicking enough?
rough: Measured thumb to rail contrast on real captures: title bar light 1.60:1, title bar dark 2.16:1, panel light 1.88:1, panel dark 2.21:1. The component page measures 1.62:1 light and 1.99:1 dark.

The page's first light rail measured 1.19:1, under the 1.5:1 you asked for, so its rail token was darkened (0.075 to 0.22) on the page and in the app. That is a change to your component page, commented where it sits.
The morph frames are drawn offscreen from the shipped control, without the glass itself: a screen capture takes longer than the 420ms move, so no real picture catches it mid-flight.

The motion is the page's own stretch and settle, applied to one system glass pane in a glass container. It is not the system's own glass-matching spring, because that spring cannot promise to stay inside the rail or overshoot by only 3 points.
Reduce Motion (a quick cross-fade) and Increase Contrast or Reduce Transparency (an opaque lighter thumb) are built but were not seen live: turning them on would change settings on your Mac.
The history bar's accent filter keeps a solid accent thumb with the same motion, not glass: white words on tinted glass would lose contrast.
The picked option's words turn bold as the move starts, not when the glass arrives. The page does the same.
